Safety Data Sheet
Aegis HydroFluid-32 Hydraulic Fluid
SDS Number: HF32-SDS-06   |   Revision Date: 2025-02-11
1. Identification
Product Name: Aegis HydroFluid-32. Recommended Use: hydraulic fluid for Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Power
Units and compatible industrial hydraulic systems. Not for use as a brake fluid or in food-grade applications.
2. Hazard Identification
Classification: Not classified as hazardous under GHS for acute toxicity. May cause mild skin irritation with
prolonged contact. Slip hazard if spilled on hard flooring.
3. Composition / Information on Ingredients
Base oil (petroleum, highly refined), 80-95%. Proprietary anti-wear and anti-oxidant additive package, 5-15%.
Exact composition withheld as a trade secret.
4. First-Aid Measures
Skin contact: wash with soap and water. Eye contact: flush with water for 15 minutes. Ingestion: do not induce
vomiting; seek medical attention.
5. Fire-Fighting Measures
Suitable extinguishing media: CO2, dry chemical, foam. Flash point (Cleveland Open Cup): approximately
210°C.
6. Accidental Release Measures
Contain spill, absorb with inert material, dispose per local regulations. Avoid release to waterways.
7. Handling and Storage
Store in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area away from oxidizing agents. Keep container closed when not in use.
8. Exposure Controls / Personal Protection
Use in well-ventilated areas. Nitrile gloves and safety glasses recommended for extended handling.
9. Physical and Chemical Properties
Appearance: clear amber liquid. Viscosity: ISO VG 32. Pour point: -33°C.

10. Stability and Reactivity
Stable under normal conditions. Avoid contact with strong oxidizers.
11. Toxicological Information
Low acute toxicity via oral, dermal, and inhalation routes based on component data.
15. Regulatory Information
Not listed as a hazardous substance under applicable regional regulations at the time of publication.
16. Other Information
This SDS covers the hydraulic fluid product only and does not describe the operation, maintenance, alarms, or
electronic control behavior of any equipment the fluid is used in. Refer to the relevant equipment manufacturer's
documentation for equipment operating procedures.
